**Finding: deviation (LOL-CAP)** — Section 7 "Limitation of Liability" (p0026–p0027).

**What the document does:** Section 7(a) is only a mutual waiver of consequential, incidental, indirect, punitive and special damages, carved out for indemnification and breach of confidentiality. There is no monetary cap — searches for "aggregate", "exceed" and "Fees" turn up no cap language anywhere in the agreement.

**Why it fails:** The fallback requires a mutual cap of 12 months' fees with carve-outs. No cap exists, so both parties (including AP) carry unlimited direct liability — a material failure, not a minor sub-element.

**Deal-specific wrinkle:** Section 5 is a revenue share in which Kubient collects from Advertisers and remits to AP; AP pays Kubient no fees. A "fees paid by Customer" cap would therefore be illusory (effectively zero) and would gut our recourse against Kubient. The redline uses the preferred greater-of construct with amounts paid or payable between the Parties plus a USD 1,000,000 floor, so the cap is meaningful in both directions.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** new Section 7(b) adding a mutual cap, an "Excluded Claims" definition (confidentiality/data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) outside the cap, and confirmation that revenue-share amounts owed are not "damages" subject to the limitation. The existing mutual consequential-damages waiver is left untouched.
